senses.gloss:
A-mūlā (‘without root’) is the name in the Atharvaveda of a plant (Methonica superba), which was used for poisoning arrows. Bloomfield, however, renders it as ‘movable property.’
Foot notes v. 314. Cf. Weber, Indische Studien, 18, 286; Whitney, Translation of the Atharvaveda, 279, accepts ‘rootless (plant).’
Hymns of the Atharvaveda, 457.
